mixup.belief: Confuses perimeter with area, multiplying length by breadth for the perimeter
signs: Says the perimeter of a 6 cm by 4 cm rectangle is 24

because.rule: shown only to a child the learner model holds this mix-up for, at this beat; any other child gets the script's own board

judge.by: a separate Claude judge (Opus), packet only, p412+l1366
judge.notes: All targets can be built on the 15x10 grid: area 40, then perimeters 26, 20 and 38. The units are right: area is 'varg ikai' and perimeter ('ghera') is 'ikai'. Every perimeter target matches a verified key (26, 20, 38). The meters show 'kshetrafal' and 'ghera' side by side, and round 2 asks for a new shape with ghera 26 right after area 40. A child who multiplies for perimeter will see the ghera meter disagree with them, which covers the mix-up. On p412 the coach line 'Grid par khet banao' is low-contrast grey but still legible, and the grid cells are small but whole. p360 was not judged (not supplied, by instruction).

judge2.by: a second separate Claude judge (Opus), packet only

faults.detail: The coach text "Grid par khet banao" is drawn over the top row of grid cells, and the goal pill "Daud 1/4 kshetrafal 40 varg ikai" butts against the bottom of the "KSHETRAFAL — / GHERA — / DAUD 1/4" pills: overlapping elements.

judge2.notes: All targets can be built on the 15x10 grid (area 40 as 8x5; perimeters 26, 20 and 38 as 8x5, 5x5 and 12x7) and match the topic keys. Building area 40 and then a different shape with perimeter 26 shows a child who multiplies for perimeter where she goes wrong. The labels are plain class-6 Hindi in Roman script ("kshetrafal", "ghera", "varg ikai"); "Daud" for round is unusual but understandable.
